binders: A finite index type ι, which is allowed to be empty.
A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A family X = (X i) indexed by ι, where each X i maps Ω to the real numbers.
Two real-valued endpoint families m and M indexed by ι.
hypotheses: For every i in ι, X i is measurable from Ω to the Borel real line.
The family (X i) is mutually independent under μ.
For every i in ι, X i(ω) belongs to the closed interval [m i, M i] for μ-almost every ω.
The threshold is strictly positive: t > 0.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of the event {ω | Σᵢ (X i(ω) − ∫ X i dμ) ≥ t} is at most exp(−2t² / Σᵢ ‖M i − m i‖²).
mathematical_definitions: For each i, the centering constant is the measure-theoretic integral Eᵢ := ∫Ω X i(y) dμ(y).
The centered sum is S(ω) := Σᵢ∈ι (X i(ω) − Eᵢ).
The denominator is V := Σᵢ∈ι ‖M i − m i‖² = Σᵢ∈ι |M i − m i|².
The tail event is Aₜ := {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t}, and its left-hand side is (μ(Aₜ)).toReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of mutually independent, measurable real-valued functions on a probability space, if each X i lies almost everywhere in the closed interval [m i, M i], then for every positive t the probability (converted to a real number) that the sum of the centered variables X i − ∫ X i dμ is at least t is no greater than exp(−2t² divided by the sum of the squared interval widths).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is finite but need not be nonempty. If it is empty, both finite sums are 0; since t > 0, the tail event is empty, while the totalized quotient has denominator 0.
The interval bounds hold μ-almost everywhere separately for each i, not pointwise for every ω.

No explicit hypotheses m i ≤ M i are present. For a populated probability space, an almost-everywhere membership hypothesis for an empty interval would be impossible, but the ordering is encoded only indirectly through that hypothesis.

The denominator V is not assumed positive. Real division in Lean is totalized, so when V = 0 the quotient (−2t²)/V evaluates using division by zero (and hence to 0 for the standard real structure), making the displayed right-hand side exp(0) = 1.
The functions are required to be independent but not identically distributed.
Only the upper-tail event with ≥ t is bounded; no lower-tail or two-sided event is stated.
The threshold restriction is strict: t must be positive.

Integrability is not an explicit hypothesis. The integral operator is nevertheless a total Lean term; the given measurability and almost-everywhere finite bounds are the assumptions relevant to establishing ordinary integrability.

The event measure is explicitly converted from an extended nonnegative real value to a real value using toReal; probability finiteness prevents an infinite event measure under the stated probability-measure hypothesis.
